erbench-syneq.source: arXiv:2606.09276v1 Table 2 (composition of the public development set) and Appendix A.3; HuggingFace EquationDiscovery/Equation_Recovery_Benchmark train.csv (columns collection, task_ID, description, scientific_field) and README.md
erbench-syneq.notes: ERBench divides its public development set into datasets (Table 2: Densities, Eponymous, Feynman, ..., PHYBench, SynEq, ...); this catalog is the whole SynEq dataset (5303 upstream rows, 5301 after symbolic-data merged 2 exact duplicates). ERBench defines no subsets inside SynEq: every row has scientific_field 'Others' and the description 'Unbiased expression of complexity N'. The generator was stratified (Appendix A.3: 200 accepted formulas per complexity 4-15, counted with sympy.count_ops, times 1-3 input variables; then filtered by a linear-regression R^2 <= 0.999 test, and 5303 selected), but these are generation strata, not named groups; the upstream rows per complexity are 4:442, 5:464, 6:448, 7:449, 8:426, 9:452, 10:418, 11:450, 12:447, 13:434, 14:423, 15:450. The 'headline'/'extended' eval_tier in the catalog metadata is symbolic-data's own label; ERBench does not use those words.

livermore2.source: dso-org/deep-symbolic-optimization dso/dso/task/regression/benchmarks.csv (current master = 2023 'uDSR release' commit 2069d4ed; NeurIPS 2021 release a49c2285 compared); Mundhenk et al. 2021, Symbolic Regression via Neural-Guided Genetic Programming Population Seeding (NeurIPS; arXiv:2111.00053) (text and Tables 2, 5, 9 checked); Landajuela et al. 2022, A Unified Framework for Deep Symbolic Regression (NeurIPS 2022 proceedings PDF) checked
livermore2.notes: The 150 problems carry their authors' group in the name: Vars2 ... Vars7, 25 each; for every key the group number equals the number of input variables (checked against n_variables). No paper describing Livermore2 was found: it does not appear in Mundhenk et al. 2021 (whose 'Livermore' set is the 22-problem catalog livermore), it is absent from that paper's NeurIPS 2021 code release (benchmarks.csv @ a49c2285 has no Livermore2 rows), and the uDSR paper (NeurIPS 2022) does not mention it; it first appears in the 2023 'uDSR release' commit of benchmarks.csv. The catalog's attribution of Livermore2 to Mundhenk et al. 2021 is therefore not supported by these sources. A wider literature search could not be completed (the web-search quota ran out), so a later paper that defines Livermore2 cannot be ruled out.

fastsrb.source: omron-sinicx/srsd-benchmark configs/datasets/feynman/{easy,medium,hard}_set.yaml and datasets/feynman.py; HuggingFace yoshitomo-matsubara/srsd-feynman_{easy,medium,hard} and srsd-feynman_{easy,medium,hard}_dummy (true_eq/ file lists); Matsubara et al. 2024, Rethinking Symbolic Regression Datasets and Benchmarks for Scientific Discovery (DMLR); viktmar/FastSRB src/expressions.yaml (difficulty field) and misc/rename_ids.md; Martinek 2025, arXiv:2508.14481
fastsrb.notes: FastSRB is SRSD-Feynman (120 problems) re-keyed to the AI Feynman names, and its expressions.yaml keeps SRSD's tier as a 'difficulty' field. The SRSD config files, the SRSD HuggingFace tier datasets, FastSRB's expressions.yaml and this catalog's difficulty field agree key for key (30 easy / 40 medium / 50 hard, no key outside a tier). SRSD names 7 of these equations differently, and FastSRB's misc/rename_ids.md gives the mapping: SRSD I.6.20, I.6.20a, I.6.20b, I.15.10, I.18.16, I.34.10, I.39.10 = keys I.6.2, I.6.2a, I.6.2b, I.15.1, I.18.14, I.34.1, I.39.1 (formulas checked against SRSD datasets/feynman.py); SRSD 'bonus.N' = key BN. Bonus equations: B8 and B18 are medium, the other 18 are hard.

subsets.name: Feynman (100)
subsets.defined_by: Udrescu & Tegmark 2020, AI Feynman: a physics-inspired method for symbolic regression (Science Advances 6(16):eaay2631; arXiv:1905.11481): the 100 main equations of the Feynman Symbolic Regression Database

feynman.source: arXiv:1905.11481 (section 'The Feynman Symbolic Regression Database'; Tables on the tested equations)
feynman.notes: The database has two sets: 100 equations from the Feynman Lectures and 20 harder 'bonus' equations from other textbooks (the separate catalog feynman-bonus). No tiers inside the 100. The key prefixes I/II/III are the Feynman Lectures volume numbers (I: 51, II: 34, III: 15), i.e. citations, not evaluation groups. SRSD's easy/medium/hard tiers cover the same equations but belong to another benchmark with different input ranges (see fastsrb), so they are not this catalog's subsets.

subsets.name: Densities

erbench-densities.source: arXiv:2606.09276v1 Table 2 (composition of the public development set) and Appendix A.3; HuggingFace EquationDiscovery/Equation_Recovery_Benchmark train.csv (columns collection, task_ID, description, scientific_field) and README.md
erbench-densities.notes: ERBench defines no subsets inside Densities. Its train.csv gives every row a scientific_field label (README: 'area of science, where expression applies'); in Densities that is Mathematics for 30 rows, Physics for 2 (densities_16 = key 'Maxwell', densities_17 = key 'Moyal') and Engineering for 1 (densities_31 = key 'fatigue life'). The paper uses these fields only to describe whole datasets (Table 2, Fields column 'EMP') and reports no results per field, so they are recorded here as information, not as subsets.

subsets.name: Livermore
subsets.defined_by: Mundhenk et al. 2021, Symbolic Regression via Neural-Guided Genetic Programming Population Seeding (NeurIPS; arXiv:2111.00053): the 'Livermore' benchmark problem set introduced in the paper (22 problems, Appendix Table 9)

subsets.name: remainder
subsets.defined_by: outside the authors' published set: rows added to benchmarks.csv in the 2023 uDSR release

livermore.source: Mundhenk et al. 2021, Symbolic Regression via Neural-Guided Genetic Programming Population Seeding (NeurIPS; arXiv:2111.00053) Sec. 4 and Appendix Tables 2, 5, 9; dso-org/deep-symbolic-optimization dso/dso/task/regression/benchmarks.csv (current master = 2023 'uDSR release' commit 2069d4ed; NeurIPS 2021 release a49c2285 compared)
livermore.notes: The paper defines Livermore as 22 problems, and its NeurIPS 2021 code release numbers them the same way. The 2023 benchmarks.csv (which the catalog follows) inserted a new Livermore-19 = log(x1^2+x1)+log(x1^3+x1) and renumbered the old 19-22 to 20-23, so paper Livermore-19/20/21/22 = catalog keys Livermore-20/21/22/23. It also added Livermore-7a and Livermore-8a, which are identical to Livermore-7 and Livermore-8 (same formula, range and function set) in both benchmarks.csv and the catalog. These three rows form the remainder subset.

subsets.name: Nguyen
subsets.defined_by: Uy et al. 2011 (GPEM 12(2)) as fixed by Petersen et al. 2021, Deep Symbolic Regression (ICLR; arXiv:1912.04871v4), Table 1/2: the 12-expression Nguyen suite

nguyen.source: Petersen et al. 2021, Deep Symbolic Regression (ICLR; arXiv:1912.04871v4) Tables 1-2; Mundhenk et al. 2021, Symbolic Regression via Neural-Guided Genetic Programming Population Seeding (NeurIPS; arXiv:2111.00053) Table 9; dso-org/deep-symbolic-optimization dso/dso/task/regression/benchmarks.csv (current master = 2023 'uDSR release' commit 2069d4ed; NeurIPS 2021 release a49c2285 compared)
nguyen.notes: Both LLNL papers treat the Nguyen problems as one suite (Mundhenk et al. 2021 Table 5 uses Nguyen-12* in place of Nguyen-12). The authors also define variants that are not in this catalog: Nguyen-12* (wider domain U(0,10,20); DSO Nguyen-12a; Mundhenk et al. 2021), Nguyen-2', 5', 8', 8'' (Petersen et al. 2021 Table 9, first set), and Nguyen^c (in catalog constant). Uy et al. 2011 itself was not checked.

subsets.name: Nguyen-c
subsets.defined_by: Petersen et al. 2021, Deep Symbolic Regression (ICLR; arXiv:1912.04871v4), Appendix Table 9, second set (Nguyen^c: Nguyen-1c, 5c, 7c, 8c, 10c)

subsets.name: remainder
subsets.defined_by: outside the authors' published set: other Constant-k rows and the Const-Test rows of dso-org/deep-symbolic-optimization dso/dso/task/regression/benchmarks.csv (current master = 2023 'uDSR release' commit 2069d4ed; NeurIPS 2021 release a49c2285 compared)

constant.source: Petersen et al. 2021, Deep Symbolic Regression (ICLR; arXiv:1912.04871v4) (v4 Table 2 and Table 9; earlier versions v1 and v2 also checked); dso-org/deep-symbolic-optimization dso/dso/task/regression/benchmarks.csv (current master = 2023 'uDSR release' commit 2069d4ed; NeurIPS 2021 release a49c2285 compared)
constant.notes: Matched by formula: Nguyen-1c = Constant-1, Nguyen-5c = Constant-2, Nguyen-10c = Constant-3, Nguyen-8c = Constant-5, Nguyen-7c = Constant-8. The authors' 'Constant' set changed between paper versions: arXiv v1 called Constant-1..4 the 'Constant benchmarks', v2 kept Constant-1..3, and the final ICLR version (v4) renamed them to the five Nguyen^c problems above. Constant-6 (x1^0.426) and Constant-7 (2 sin(1.3 x1) cos(x2)) appear in none of these versions, and Constant-4 (2.7 x1^x2) only in v1. Const-Test-1 and Const-Test-2 (both pi x1^2, differing only in the DSO function set) are repository test rows. If srbf prefers the repository's name groups instead, the split would be Constant-1..8 and Const-Test-1..2.

subsets.name: PhySO astrophysics laws
subsets.defined_by: Tenachi, Ibata & Diakogiannis 2023 (arXiv:2303.03192), Appendix A

physo-astro.source: arXiv:2303.03192v2 Sec. V (V.2, V.4) and Appendix A
physo-astro.notes: The paper presents its examples as one 'panel of astrophysical test cases' (Sec. V): expansion-law is the case study of Sec. V.2 and nfw-profile is one of the 'additional toy test cases' of Sec. V.4; it defines no subsets for evaluation. The panel's other cases are excluded or deduplicated by the catalog (see its exclusions note).
